decision: Under the stated canonical-output-only constraints, local boundary editing does not add feasible evidence outputs beyond all-atom selection. Close representation-expansion as a standalone mechanism claim, while separating contextual scoring, finite resource allocation and search bias as unproven estimands.

freeze_order_static_review.interpretation: Fixture/source bindings are written before enumeration and rendering calls. Imports occur earlier; no independent execution-order instrumentation was performed.

item_cap_counterexample.note: Tests pre-merge item-cap representability with a nonbinding final budget; it is not a measured quality effect.

limits: Finite synthetic enumeration validates this implementation on these fixed cases; the general theorem still rests on the constructive coarse-to-fine expansion proof.

Positive budgets512 and4096 are nonbinding for all64 enumerated complete strings (maximum507bytes); budget0 checks empty-only behavior. No tight positive-byte or token-budget behavior is empirically established.
Costs are UTF-8 evidence-block bytes, not tokenizer counts, HTTP payload bytes or billing.
No scorer/selector quality, runtime search completeness, latency, natural coverage, semantic support or answer gains follow from family inclusion.
Only the five explicitly frozen sources were rehashed; no claim of a full transitive imported-source closure.
Backend/network denial and zero-resource record were inspected statically, not re-executed by this reviewer.
execution_audit.method: Independent standard-library enumeration using whole-block membership predicates, character-set connected components and literal canonical rendering; no production helpers imported.

claims_and_proof.claim: If Q refines P, then F(P) is a subset of F(Q).
claims_and_proof.proof: Take any feasible coarse selection J. Select every fine cell contained in each selected coarse cell. The refinement definition makes this fine selection have exactly U(J). Its normal-form intervals, IDs, full rendered string, measured budget and final run count are therefore identical. Thus every feasible coarse output remains feasible under Q. No additive or monotone cost assumption is required.

claims_and_proof.claim: The all-atom partition A contains every legal atom-boundary partition output family: F(P) subset F(A).
claims_and_proof.proof: The atomic partition refines each legal partition P, so apply the previous statement. If the permitted partition class includes A, the union of all F(P) equals F(A). A stricter budget can make refinement inclusion non-strict.

claims_and_proof.claim: Equal coverage produces equal complete outputs under this canonical renderer contract.
claims_and_proof.proof: Equal source-coordinate sets have the same unique maximal-interval normal form. Source/version/context and the metadata rule are fixed, so all fields and text bytes rendered from that form agree. Merely equal passage wording or equal non-whitespace coordinates is insufficient.

claims_and_proof.claim: Changing only atom-boundary grouping cannot enlarge the all-atom representable feasible family.
claims_and_proof.proof: Any legal grouped selection expands to an equivalent atomic selection. This says nothing about which member a finite algorithm finds, its scoring quality, model-call cost or search complexity.

definitions.atoms: Finite nonempty pairwise-disjoint half-open intervals A_i. Their union D is the fixed selectable source domain.
definitions.family: F(P) = {Z(U(J)) : J subset P and U(J) is feasible}. This is a representable-output family, not a family of outputs actually reached by a particular scorer/search routine.
definitions.feasibility: Feasible iff count(Z(U)) <= B and len(N(U)) <= R. The counter/tokenizer/version and fixed prompt context are identical; neither pre-merge item count nor intermediate greedy state imposes an additional constraint.
definitions.legal_partition: P groups whole atoms without adding/removing source coordinates. Every chunk is exactly the union of its member atoms. If a chunk must be a single contiguous source slice, it may group only coordinate-touching atoms inside one connected component of D.
definitions.normal_form: N(U) is the source-ordered list of maximal connected half-open intervals, merging touching selected spans and never filling a positive-length unselected gap.
definitions.output: Z(U) is the complete deterministic renderer output from N(U), source substrings and fixed context. IDs are assigned from canonical final source spans/document version after merging. All other visible metadata must be fixed or a deterministic function of U/source, not of pre-merge cells, grouping, scores, ranks, provenance lists or call history.
definitions.refinement: Q refines P iff every p in P is exactly the disjoint union of cells of Q. Every cell in either partition remains selectable without independent label/score filtering.
definitions.selection: Any subset J of partition cells. U(J) is their union of source coordinates. Empty-selection handling is identical across partitions.
definitions.source: One fixed source string S, document/version identity, and Python-character coordinate system. Equality of coverage means equality of all covered source coordinates, including whitespace; equal wording alone is not equal occurrence coverage.

falsifiability.diagnostic_order: If a purported counterexample appears, first inspect domain gaps, pre-merge item limits, candidate eligibility, canonical metadata and whether feasibility was tested only on final output. Do not reinterpret a failed greedy search as missing representability.
falsifiability.representation_test: For a fixed finite synthetic domain and two partitions satisfying the assumptions, every feasible coarse output must appear byte-identically among all fine-subset canonical outputs. A missing byte-identical output falsifies an implementation claim of this contract.

limits: This is an elementary set-refinement/canonicalization argument, not a new algorithm or an exhaustive novelty claim.
It does not assert natural annotation coverage, semantic support, answer accuracy, learned score calibration, causal utility or natural effect sizes.

It does not claim that the current production exporter/enrichment/index/renderer already obey the canonical output assumptions; the prior source audit found grouping-dependent owner/path and ordinal IDs.

A boundary proposal can still alter scorer inputs, search bias, retrieval/index features and cost; such effects must be identified explicitly instead of described as expanding the fixed all-atom feasible family.

minimal_counterexample.failure: Coarse may select its one cell to output [0:2]ab. Fine would need both cells and violates the item cap, although those two cells would merge into one final run. Therefore coarse-family inclusion fails.
minimal_counterexample.rendering: Render each final maximal interval as [start:end] followed by the exact substring; budget B=100 characters is nonbinding.
minimal_counterexample.restored_case: Remove the item cap and keep only B=100/final R=1: selecting both fine atoms emits exactly [0:2]ab, restoring inclusion.
minimal_counterexample.status: Analytical authored counterexample; no implementation or model executed.
minimal_counterexample.violated_assumption: A pre-merge selected-item cap is imposed in addition to final run cap.

necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.illustration: With source axb and domain atoms [0,1) and [2,3), an alleged coarse slice [0,3) adds x. It is not a legal grouping of the fixed domain. Either forbid crossing this gap or represent the grouped object as the two original intervals. Sorting by atom ordinal alone does not establish source adjacency.
necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.requirement: Do not replace a union by its convex hull when it includes excluded coordinates.

necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.consequence: Identical coverage can otherwise yield different complete strings and costs, so neither output identity nor preservation of a budget test follows.
necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.requirement: Canonicalize final source-span IDs after merging; do not retain item ordinal, parent/owner IDs, path chosen by original chunks, candidate scores, per-item labels or candidate counts in the rendered output unless derived solely from final coverage.

necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.consequence: Partition-dependent filtering or limited scorer admission can delete fine choices; that is a changed effective candidate domain, not a counterexample to the theorem as defined.
necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.requirement: All atomic cells needed to expand every coarse block must remain eligible. Keep the source domain fixed before any scored top-M/no-label threshold.

necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.consequence: A scorer evaluating whole blocks can prefer different coverage from an atom scorer, even though both operate inside the same abstract output family. This can matter operationally and is not ruled out by the theorem.
necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.requirement: Scores may be partition-dependent as an objective, but cannot silently become extra feasibility constraints or visible output fields.

necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.consequence: Greedy ranking, top-k candidate truncation, no-revisit decisions, time/call caps or intermediate run/budget rejection can prevent an algorithm from reaching a feasible fine selection. Full-render costs need not be monotone as items coalesce. The theorem does not certify any existing selector as complete.
necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.requirement: The family definition ranges over all subsets and tests the final merged output.

necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.consequence: An all-atom representation can have a much larger search space or more scoring calls than a coarse partition. Equal feasible expressivity does not imply equal efficiency or attainable quality under a computation budget.
necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.requirement: Keep computational/resource claims separate from representation.

necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.consequence: Splitting inside an original atom, recovering previously excluded evidence, changing retrieval augmentation, rewriting text or retaining boundary-specific metadata changes an assumption and requires a separate comparison.
necessary_assumptions_and_failure_modes.requirement: Source, atomic boundary basis, candidate domain and full-render contract remain fixed.

mathematical_review.verdict: The proposed inclusion theorem is valid for canonical source-coverage output feasibility under the assumptions below. Merely fixing nonoverlapping atoms and allowing atom-index split/merge is insufficient unless blocks cannot fill excluded source gaps.

gate_decision.continue_condition: Name exactly one remaining estimand and the cheapest contrast that isolates it from the known context, routing and search explanations, with an observable failure outcome and independent utility when utility is claimed.
gate_decision.current_proposal: Fixed-domain query-conditioned split/merge plus canonical selected-source coalescing has not identified an additional output capability or a distinct new research mechanism.
gate_decision.stop_condition: If the only claimed addition is query-conditioned boundaries, a new teacher, source-faithful rendering, hard final budgets or a new name for all-atom selection/coalescing, do not expand scoring or train a boundary student on that basis.

mechanism_gate.historical_document_boundary: GRANULARITY_PARENT_CONTROL is a dated pre-execution amendment. Its no-fresh-scores and pending-run statements are not treated as current execution status.
mechanism_gate.literature_boundary: Closest-work statements are based only on the two specified existing reports and their recorded primary-paper sections. No new primary-page access or exhaustive novelty search was performed; no first/new/unexplored claim is made.
null_and_identification: Two boundary configurations with the same canonical complete generation request and model settings have no boundary-specific effect on the conditional response distribution. Any independently sampled output variation is not evidence for a boundary preference.
A teacher preference between output-equivalent configurations cannot by itself certify independent downstream utility; it may reflect scoring presentation or nuisance metadata.

Multiple boundary configurations may realize the same output. Supervision must retain these equivalence classes or explicitly target proposal cost/search behavior instead of pretending there is one uniquely useful boundary.
The existing 117 single-unit judgments do not directly label local split/merge utility, resource savings or causal downstream benefit.

remaining_estimands.failure_condition: If the gain is reproduced by an ordinary fixed parent/window context or only reflects a different returned source range, this does not establish a distinct learned boundary mechanism.
remaining_estimands.known_overlap: Existing report already identifies contextual fine-grained representations, query-to-granularity routing and child-score-to-parent retrieval. Choosing JEV or calling the scorer a boundary teacher does not distinguish the mechanism.
remaining_estimands.name: context_conditioned_scoring
remaining_estimands.necessary_evidence: A predeclared independently assessed utility difference, including harmful and unchanged-output cases, that remains beyond teacher self-scores and beyond simple context/granularity baselines. Coverage-only evidence supports only coverage claims, not answer quality.
remaining_estimands.question: On the same available source and final output family, does scoring a target with an explicitly defined local context select higher independent-utility canonical evidence than scoring it alone or with a fixed parent/window context?
remaining_estimands.required_contrast: Separate scoring-context variation from output-range and search variation. Retain the same final renderer, budget, source exposure and declared scoring-resource allowance; compare against fixed-context and existing parent/granularity controls. Bind fresh scores to the actual changed scoring input.

remaining_estimands.failure_condition: If savings come only from fewer exposed candidates, larger uncounted scoring contexts or a simpler route matching the tradeoff, no distinct mechanism has been shown.
remaining_estimands.known_overlap: Utility/cost-trained query-dependent granularity planning is already covered in the existing literature gate. A boundary parameterization must contribute beyond a different implementation of that allocation problem.
remaining_estimands.name: finite_scoring_resource_allocation
remaining_estimands.necessary_evidence: A useful utility-versus-resource tradeoff on prospectively fixed cases, against simple hierarchical/routing and child-score baselines, not just a lower count of nominal chunks or API requests.
remaining_estimands.question: At the same declared total scoring cost, can a boundary-based proposal policy reach higher independent utility, or reach the same utility with less scoring, than simple granularity routing and fine-unit alternatives?
remaining_estimands.required_contrast: Match the cost definition, full input/output cost where relevant, available cache and source exposure. Count proposal/context construction, failed calls and inference overhead; separate offline training cost from online amortized cost. Do not compare a paid proposal policy to artificially rescored cache-reusable atoms.

remaining_estimands.failure_condition: If matching revisit/grouped actions or a simple route eliminates the effect, the evidence supports the simpler search explanation, not a distinct boundary model.
remaining_estimands.known_overlap: Grouping, hierarchical expansion and greedy-search fixes are familiar mechanisms. Beating one particular single-pass atom order alone is not evidence of new chunking capacity or SLAC-specific novelty.
remaining_estimands.name: search_inductive_bias
remaining_estimands.necessary_evidence: On tiny synthetic domains an independently enumerated feasible optimum can expose reachable-set/regret differences; that establishes a solver property only. A research utility claim additionally needs independent utility and a matched-budget baseline on prospective cases.
remaining_estimands.question: Within the identical canonical feasible-output family and scoring objective, do learned local bundles or boundary proposals find higher-utility outputs under the same search/evaluation allowance?
remaining_estimands.required_contrast: Separate score quality from search by holding a complete objective table fixed where possible. Compare against simple grouping/routing and adequate atom search including the already exposed revisit confound; report final canonical output identity, not just scalar metric ties.

representation_result.equality_condition: If the allowed partition family includes the singleton-atom partition, the union of all partition feasible-output sets equals the all-atom feasible-output set. For an individual coarser partition there is generally inclusion only.
limits: This does not show that an actual fixed-score single-pass atom greedy algorithm achieves every feasible output or outperforms a chunk-group proposal algorithm.

A grouped candidate can add several atoms in one admissible transition while an atomwise intermediate prefix fails run or nonmonotone token constraints; this is a search-action difference, not extra representational capacity.
Stable source IDs alone do not prove equal final strings: the actual renderer also exposes IDs, paths, ranks, scores and other metadata. Canonicalizing just the text or span is insufficient.

Production evidence selection caps records and does not perform the research script touching-span coalescing. The theorem is a controlled research contract, not an established invariant of all current production routes.

New internal-atom cuts, rewritten/compressed text, imported neighboring source, a changed retrieval domain or alternate visible contextual annotations change the premise and must be identified as a different intervention.
necessary_assumptions: Every edit boundary is an atom endpoint and every atom in every eligible selected partition chunk is available to the all-atom selector.
Both arms preserve exactly the same source characters and use the same ordering and touching-only union; neither fills source gaps or rewrites text.

The renderer and all visible metadata are deterministic functions of the query and canonical source runs, independent of partition, candidate provenance, scoring unit IDs, ordinal chunk IDs, ranks or scores.
The same deterministic full-render cost and same final run cap apply. There is no additional atom-count cap or intermediate-prefix constraint in the feasible-output definition.
All other generation messages, model settings and downstream conditions are held fixed when interpreting equal evidence output as equal model input.
representation_result.proof: For any selected chunk set S from P, select exactly the atoms whose intervals form those chunks. Its source union is identical, hence C(S) is identical. Under the common canonical renderer the entire evidence string and its measured cost are identical and the final run count is identical. Thus every feasible partition-selected canonical output is feasible in the all-atom family. Tokenizer monotonicity or additivity is unnecessary because the compared rendered strings are equal.
representation_result.setup: Let A be a fixed finite ordered family of disjoint positive source intervals covering the allowed source domain. Each eligible partition P groups consecutive touching atoms; it neither cuts inside an atom nor imports text across an excluded gap. C maps any selected intervals to their ordered maximal touching union runs.

next_step: Zero-model design and bounded natural witness screening for contextual scoring: same exposed source information and fixed-window control; distinguish scorer-only context from information delivered to the answerer. Do not reopen the two-question packing variants or issue new scoring calls before that gate.
